name: Chip Roy

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: THE EMPIRE IS STRIKING BACK
statements.title: THE EMPIRE IS STRIKING BACK
sentences: We could be debating right now a bill to ban congressional stock trading among Members of Congress so they do not enrich themselves when they vote on the matters they were sent here to vote upon.

The empire is that which gave us the $42 trillion of debt, the rampant growth of the bureaucracy, the regulatory state that crushes small business, the laws and regulations and rules that favor corporate America over small business Main Street, and the average American family, and everybody knows this is true.

So what is going to stop a big, bloated bill that is going to be a Christmas tree to put a bunch of legislation on it and spend money on defense that is unpaid for without, by the way, a serious debate ever in this Chamber--as my friend from Kentucky often raises--about war powers.
This Congress has never voted on what is going on in Iran.
My friend from Kentucky would argue we have had some votes on War Powers Resolutions, and he would be correct.
Some of us struggle with those votes because we don't like to vote in the negative because the war powers construct is, frankly, reversed.

With all due respect to this administration, which has done a number of things of which I am proud and I support, it is a part of that empire striking back right now, wanting a massive plus-up in defense spending.

I am not in for a blank check to use, in the name of war, the power of government to target the American people, to rack up debt, and to be used as an excuse by my colleagues on the other side of the aisle to have an expansive welfare state in trade for defense spending, because that is what is coming.
The election wasn't just about the Iran war and diesel and gas prices.

The richest city in the world is living off of the back of this God- forsaken town, and the God-forsaken people in this body and in the other body that spend money that they don't have to rack up debt, to bankrupt our kids and grandkids, while the people in this town get rich off of the back of it, including the defense lobbyists who no doubt right now really want a massive defense spending bill, including all the insurance companies and all the hospitals that right now want to get rich off of whatever this body and the Senate and this administration are going to do in the name of healthcare.
Do you think Medicare for All is about helping people?
ObamaCare was a complete and total failure.
It is not about getting the stock trading bill on the floor.
It is not about passing a term limits bill.

We had stipulated for the entirety of this Congress that we should pass a codification of President Trump's border security policies that were reflected in H.R. 2 in the previous Congress: That is, stop the abuse of parole, stop the abuse of asylum, stop catch and release, stop the abuse of unaccompanied alien children.

I have colleagues in this Chamber who campaign on border security, go home to their districts and talk about border security, but refused to do the thing we told them we would do, which is to codify and change the law to secure the border of the United States, and they failed.
I will be very clear for everybody observing what is about to happen in December.
When we have heard from our leadership, we won't do a Christmas tree omnibus bill before Christmas.
There is bad stuff going on, so you must vote this way or we are going to do it anyway.
The rule is when the majority says: ``Hey, this is what we are going to put on the House floor,'' and they put it altogether, and they put it on the House floor.

Now, I am willing to wager what little congressional salary I have left for the remainder of this year with any of my colleagues if they want to come down to the floor of the House--I don't think they will, but I will debate anybody on the floor of the House anytime your position of why we shouldn't do that and why I shouldn't have stood up to say we are not going to pass this rule if we are not going to do the things we told the American people we were going to do.
I am going to leave the Chamber, for now, but I am not leaving the body politic.
I can assure you, for my remaining 45 days, I am going to use it that way.
I don't know whether I will be able to come back to the House floor again before this body closes down.
I will be here every day until January 3 if the body is open.
I could start naming them, but I am going to leave them out.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: MATH PROBLEM
statements.title: MATH PROBLEM
sentences: But in a republican form of government where we are charged with following the Constitution and following the duty to lead this country forward on behalf of those constituents, that we have to make the tough choices here to be able to say to our people that if you want to have low inflation, low interest rates, if you don't want to have the tax of massive debt hung around the necks of your children, you are going to have to understand that we are going to have to make tough choices here.
Mr. Speaker, I thank the gentleman for his stalwart determination to focus on fiscal responsibility and to do the right thing.

I will note for the people watching in Arizona-1 that elected you for a number of terms before you decided to run for another office as I did, that you have been stalwart and consistent in being down here on the floor of the House of Representatives talking about this issue for the entirety of your career.
We are going to do what we need to do for the people and for the country, not just to buy votes to be sent back to power.
I thank him for it, and I hope I will see him on the floor again.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: ADDRESSING VOTERS' NEEDS
statements.title: ADDRESSING VOTERS' NEEDS
sentences: I have tried to work across the aisle and work within the Conference, as Republicans, to actually address the concerns and the needs of the American people and to do our job, in a republican form of government, to actually follow the Constitution, to actually address unlimited spending and the national debt of $42 trillion, to actually secure the border of the United States, to actually put in place permanent reform, to actually stand up for the hardworking men and women of this country who actually make this world work.
That same month, Microsoft applied for 150,000 more H-1B visas because it can't find qualified Americans.
You think to yourself how the Iran war has made everything expensive, but at least we're stopping their nuclear bomb.
You weren't even sure where Iran was until you googled it after we first bombed them in March.
Now a Republican surrogate, the daughter of a Governor or the wife of an elderly billionaire, explains that young White men are the real welfare queens.
They'd rather play video games in their parents' basements than work.

I am here to tell you that he is speaking for an entire Nation of people who are tired of a town that they rightly perceive as being in the hip pocket of too much of the oligarchy, too many of the billionaires and ruling class, or--as my friend Jeff Sessions used to say in the Senate--the masters of the universe, the people who make all the decisions.
People are talking about data centers and AI and the need to beat China.
Then they watch Nvidia's CEO embroiled in scandal and see how everybody is patting each other on the back, helping each other in the billionaire class and the ruling class gathering together.

The average American is sitting in their hometown saying: I don't want a data center in my backyard that is going to suck up my water and my electricity, that is going to be processing computing that addicts my children to porn and sports gambling, while we ruin college sports and all the things that we enjoy on the weekend to take a break from this godforsaken political ruling class that is sticking it to us again.
But I also have colleagues who think it is just the war, who think it is just because of Iran, otherwise everything else would have been hunky-dory.
You can't just dismiss it and say, oh, pay the higher gas prices so we can beat Iran.

With all due respect to the President and with all due respect to every vote we have taken on the floor of the House on war powers put forward by my colleagues that put us in the defensive posture of having to vote against our troops in the field that the Commander in Chief has put in the field, the President never came to us and asked us.

We never earned the people's backing to send our blood and our treasure into Iran for our national security interests, even if the case is strong to do it, even if cutting the head of the snake in Iran is worth it, even if knocking out the proxy terrorists is worth it, even if taking out their nuclear capability and conventional capability is worth it.

It is not just the concerns about the money floating around and AI and data centers, and it is not just the concern that Calley is raising about MAHA, whatever is going on at the Kennedy Center and the grift, whatever is happening with Ambassadors to Greece and the grift, whatever is happening with numerous people, you go down the line, and as I said putting at the top of the ticket of the biggest Republican State in the Nation someone who is indicted and impeached by the Republican Texas House.

None of the people that signed their death warrant, pledging their lives or fortunes and their sacred honor, were doing so for corporate interests and so corporate boards could tell their great-great-great-great-grandchildren that there are six genders or that they have to get in line with some corporate interest or they have to work for the profit of some billionaire over them.
Oh, if we had just not done Iran, we were just sailing along.

Mom-and-pop shops can't compete with the lawyers who know when the next road is going to go in and the next thing is going to be taken with eminent domain and the next data center is going to be put in so that H-1B workers can fill those positions and that, as I said, you can be addicted to porn and sports gambling.

I will tell you that I do not direct my ire or my frustration at the people, because I think the people were trying to send a loud message, as they have been doing now for several cycles, that this town is not doing what it is supposed to do.
Look, I have something here that I want to read--and I am going to paraphrase; it was tweeted on election day--that captures part of the problem.

And upstairs, the son you sacrificed everything for is lying awake in the bedroom that he slept in at 12, wondering what the heck he's supposed to do with his life now, and whether--I am going to paraphrase--he can achieve the American Dream.
I will be leaving the House come January.
I am going to stay in the fight because it is a fight that we have to have.
Well, we have to decide what it is we are fighting for.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: HYDE AMENDMENT'S 50TH ANNIVERSARY
statements.title: HYDE AMENDMENT'S 50TH ANNIVERSARY
sentences: They weren't talking about getting abortions.
Now, 50-odd years removed from Roe, obviously we celebrated the decision by the Court in Dobbs, but abortion continues.

Fifty years ago, Congressman Hyde, Judiciary Committee Chairman Hyde eventually, one of the more eloquent statesmen that this body has ever known, led on this issue, and we have had now for 50 years, as we are celebrating today, the Hyde amendment, which was a commonsense, bipartisan understanding that taxpayers shouldn't be forced to fund something abhorrent to their faith and abhorrent to the values that any sense of humanity and decency would suggest you shouldn't have to fund.
I am proud that in the One Big Beautiful Bill Act, we had a provision in there that stopped funding from going to Planned Parenthood for a year.
That is a good thing because funds are fungible, and we all know that money was flowing to Planned Parenthood for the purpose of ultimately exterminating life.

It is not victorious when tonight a woman's life is in danger and a baby's life is going to be terminated through a pill circulating through the mail of the United States Postal Service or through various forms of transit, all still being allowed by our own Federal Government.
The American taxpayer should not be forced to subsidize the abortion industry directly or indirectly.
I will be looking down on you from above.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: AMERICANS ARE ASKING QUESTIONS
statements.title: AMERICANS ARE ASKING QUESTIONS
sentences: Gasoline prices and diesel prices continue to go up and rise as the war in Iran rages on.

But for conservatives and but for the Freedom Caucus, we would not have reduced spending on welfare, Medicaid, and the various programs ripe with fraud that are racking up mountains of debt and causing the American people to have to spend much more in inflation.
But for the Freedom Caucus, we would not have eliminated a tax on guns that infringe on our Second Amendment right.
But for the House Freedom Caucus, we would not have made the tax cuts permanent all the way through.
But for the House Freedom Caucus, we would not have passed the Laken Riley Act, with the SUE Act in it, giving power to States to sue the Federal Government if they fail to secure the border.
But for the House Freedom Caucus, we would not have gotten a 5-year ban on a central bank digital currency, to protect you from surveillance.

Going back to the American people who are still struggling to afford life, I don't care what billionaire I piss off when I tell them that the American people are suffering right now because they can't afford a home or because they can't afford their food or they can't afford a car because we want to have another safety device in the car or another regulation in the car or a surveillance apparatus, like a kill switch, in the car.
You want to know why they are mad about data centers?
I will tell you why they are mad about data centers.

Some esoteric defense against the arms race against China, so I can have a concrete box outside of my small town in west Texas that is filled with computers that are being operated by people on H-1B visas from India, that are chock-full of all sorts of searches for child pornography and hooking kids on porn or betting on college sports, while we turn college sports upside down and make it basically professional.
Then even the most important and the smartest people in the world tell our people: You are not going to have a job in 10 years because robots and AI are going to take your jobs away.
Why do you think the American people are in revolt to data centers popping up at every corner in America?
I can promise you that as secure as the border is, because of the great work of the Trump administration, we have not codified a darn thing in this Chamber.

They were going to just gloss over a bill that we have to codify the President's policies of securing the border, stopping the abuse of asylum, stopping the abuse of parole, stopping catch and release, stopping the abuse of unaccompanied children, all of these things that led directly to the deaths of Americans like Laken Riley, like Jocelyn Nungaray, and countless others.

We haven't addressed birthright citizenship after the United States Supreme Court made up out of whole cloth nonsense that the 14th Amendment says that if you are born here, literally of a mother pregnant who comes here across the Rio Grande River or flies into Miami and has a baby, you are a citizen.
It is a fiction, and we shouldn't let the United States Supreme Court make up a fiction and then follow it and dismantle our country in the process.
The fact of the matter is that decision enables one of the most pervasive illegal immigration magnets that is destroying our country.
We should not entertain importing one more person until we secure our border for good.
If we aren't serious about securing the border, then what are we doing?
We will never have a secure border if we don't pass the bills we said we would pass.
If we aren't serious about cutting spending, with a national debt of $40 trillion, we will never solve the inflation crisis that pervades us today.
If we are not serious about codifying President Trump's border policies, we can't expect our border to be secure rather than descending into chaos as soon as the Democrats take power.

If we are not serious about passing the SAVE America Act, which we passed three times in this body and the Senate refused to pass, how can you stand up and say that you believe that only American citizens should vote in American elections and we should have voter ID federally?
We have the obligation to stand up for something more important as this whole debate of AI, this whole debate of data centers.

I don't want those people to tell me I have to have some sort of data center or have to have some sort of way of living that isn't consistent with what I think God gave to us to have dominion and control over.
If we are not serious about those things, we will lose the country.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: STOP INSIDER TRADING ACT
statements.title: STOP INSIDER TRADING ACT
sentences: I have a right to trade stocks.
Yes, I had legislation that would have required divestiture.
Obviously, I am the lead author also of the SAVE America Act.
I am not going to debate that here because right now we are talking about this bill addressing stock trading.
I will say one thing that I think merits being said: I think we should be having a straight up-or-down vote on this stock trading bill.
I am not done this year demanding that we have a straight up-or-down vote on stock trading.
You can't, whether you are on this or that side of the aisle, hide behind the SAVE America Act for your opposition to what we need to do to change the culture of this institution.
I am going to end up voting for this because I support both measures.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: NATIONAL SECURITY, DEPARTMENT OF STATE, AND RELATED PROGRAMS APPROPRIATIONS ACT, 2027
statements.title: NATIONAL SECURITY, DEPARTMENT OF STATE, AND RELATED PROGRAMS APPROPRIATIONS ACT, 2027
sentences: The bill continues to fund millions of dollars for the United Nations, despite longstanding concerns over anti-Israel bias, corruption, peacekeeper misconduct, institutional failure, and ways in which the United Nations operates on a regular basis in direct contradiction to the interests of the United States.

It has stood up in solidarity with the worst and most evil countries in the world against our interests and dared to wag their finger at the United States, built on the back of our funding and generosity and, by the way, real estate, to give them a platform to target us and to target our interests, in addition to constantly and consistently going after our friends in Israel.
Madam Chair, I urge adoption of the amendment to ensure taxpayer dollars are spent on advancing American interests, not funding institutions that too often work against them.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: PEOPLE OF TEXAS STEPPING UP
statements.title: PEOPLE OF TEXAS STEPPING UP
sentences: It was difficult in working through all the complexities of the tax policy, dealing with the complexities of the reforms to Medicaid, to welfare programs, saving $1.7 trillion, pulling back some of the subsidies and unreliable power that was so critically important.
They were people who were camping with their families, whole families that were swept down the river.

We raised over $150 million in private contributions, of which over half, pushing $80 million to $100 million, had been pushed out the door--the rest of it should be out the door by the end of this year--to help small businesses, to help people keep afloat, mental health, keeping people in houses and apartments, giving people the ability to stay on their feet, and all done through the power of the strong faith of the people of Texas.

The number of people who volunteered, I came in on the night of the Fourth of July, and I went to the facility where they were gathering in all of the experts and all the people who were there and all the volunteers, and the sheriff and all the local law enforcement.
I want to talk about the Supreme Court ruling today, because it matters a great deal.
Today, the United States Supreme Court issued an opinion that I believe was profoundly misguided and undermines our national security and our sovereignty as a nation in a profoundly damaging way.
This is the issue of so-called birthright citizenship.

This opinion today by the United States Supreme Court, saying that the 14th Amendment, which was very clearly ratified to deal with the issue of slavery in a post-slavery world--to whom do these former slaves now owe allegiance?

For five Supreme Court Justices today to manufacture in whole cloth that the 14th Amendment, ratified in 1868, somehow conferred upon someone citizenship because a parent came to the United States and birthed the child on American soil, despite not being a citizen and despite not having any allegiance to the United States, is not just appalling, but it begs: Who we are as a nation?

The Chief Justice, no doubt, and Justice Barrett, and the other three Justices who joined that opinion no doubt believe they were doing some sort of great service by trying to establish that this means some great thing for the United States.

If you are telling the world that all you have to do is flout our laws and break our laws, come to our country and have a child, and that child gets to have citizenship, which has things conferred upon it--voting and other privileges and access to welfare benefits--then all of those who bled and died for this great Nation, to just hand that over in violation of the entire text, spirit, and letter of the Constitution and the 14th Amendment, is detrimental to our republican form of government.

Roberts, emphasizing: Children born of parents unlawfully or temporarily present in the United States satisfy both elements of the Citizenship Clause under the Constitution, he concluded, they are citizens at birth.
The Supreme Court majority ruled that illegal aliens invading our country, having U.S.-born children, and is somehow legally sound even though the Justices in Wong Kim Ark rejected that notion.
This is something that has been debated for a long time, but when we think about this, an estimated 124,000 to 300,000 anchor babies--which are children born to illegal aliens--are born each year.
In 2023, up to 250,000 children were born to illegal aliens, which accounted for 7 percent of total births.
The fact is, the United States Congress cannot just sit idly by and allow the Supreme Court to do this.
The Supreme Court is going to get the final word on what the law is.
Well, I would tell you that the Supreme Court has clearly made significant errors in judgment in the past.
There have been other opinions, Roe v. Wade, which the Court has now rightly gone in a different direction.

I would argue, though, that the Congress needs to react swiftly and make very clear that we define what ``subject to the jurisdiction thereof'' means, that Congress should act swiftly to say we are not going to fund this false notion of who citizens are; and, thirdly, that we are going to just pause immigration.

If the Supreme Court of the United States, in its infinite wisdom, says they get to decide as the final arbiter who is or is not a citizen, then why should Congress allow people to come into the United States to abuse it, to have children, to take advantage of a citizenship that is not actually allowed under the Constitution because the Supreme Court got it wrong?

If the Supreme Court were to order or interpret the law that the President of the United States or the Speaker of the House or the majority leader of the Senate needs to appear before them unclothed to report to the Supreme Court, should those leaders of the other branches comply?
Well, if the Supreme Court issues a ruling that is patently and factually unconstitutional, must the other branches follow it?
This Congress better fix this because I have no interest in continuing to fund the operations of a government that has been undermined by the United States Supreme Court.
Well, let's keep having that fight, too, because the SAVE America Act is not the actual full nature of the fight.

Here we are at a time when this body, Congress--the House and the Senate together--need to act to protect our Nation's sovereignty: By allowing only American citizens to vote in American elections; to require voter identification in elections of our Federal officials; to, yes, make very clear that ``subject to the jurisdiction thereof'' means what it means; and, no, we are not going to import people into the United States as long as we are being told absolutely you must grant citizenship for any child born here.

We can also codify what the President has been doing to secure our border to stop the abuse of the American people that was happening under Biden and Mayorkas by codifying--as we did under H.R. 2 in the last Congress--that work, stop the abuse of asylum, stop the abuse of parole, stop the abuse of catch- and-release policies and all the policies that were being abused to undermine our country which, by the way, is also tied to the birthright citizenship issue.

However, when our country has been badly exploited for decades, when there are people here right now who want to destroy the United States, who want it to become an Islamic state, who want to milk our welfare benefits, commit fraud against the country, and who don't want to raise the American flag with the flag of another country, I do not understand for the life of me why we do not continue to do what we are doing by this President and remove people and why this Congress will not act right now, immediately, to respond to the Supreme Court.

You cannot tell me, Mr. Speaker, that Jefferson and Adams, both so central to both the drafting of the Declaration of Independence and its adoption by the Continental Congress on July 2 by a vote, July 4 by drafting, in 1776 to then pass both 50 years to the day on July 4, 2026, with Adams passing saying: Jefferson lives, only to find out, in truth, Jefferson had passed.
I am going to first, though, focus a little bit on my home State of Texas.
Now, so many of us are going to remember July Fourth there in Kerrville for that event, but I am going to be back in Kerrville this Fourth of July.
I am going to go back to Kerrville because I want to be with the people who I represent, and I am proud to represent them as the Congressman for the 21st Congressional District.
I don't know if I will ever do that again, but certainly not in a building that was pretty much empty except for me and three staffers.
I am going to make a quick political commentary here and then come back to our celebration of the 250th.

Look, I can tell you right now that for the decisions I have remaining in my time in Congress in this term, for the remainder of our funding decisions and appropriations, for whatever we are going to do in reconciliation, we better fix this.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: REPUBLICAN UPDATE
statements.title: REPUBLICAN UPDATE
sentences: The President came in and didn't need changes to the law to do the work of actually securing the border and did so.

He did so with the great men and women of ICE and Border Patrol and the leadership of Tom Homan, the now two Secretaries of Homeland Security, and other patriots who were working to secure the border, and they brought it to a complete standstill.

We are no longer living in fear that more criminals are coming across so that the Jocelyn Nungarays of the world get murdered and taken from us as did Laken Riley in my friend's home State of Georgia.

You are seeing people who want to be a part of the military because the President has removed the absurdity of the woke agenda and the DEI and all this stuff, taking their eyes off the ball of becoming the best fighting force in the world.
It is this President that took on the cartels and declared them as the terrorist organizations that they are.

It is this President that took on Maduro and went after the change that needed to occur in Venezuela so we no longer had that pressure point that was facilitating our enemies in China and in Russia, that was reestablishing our footprint in the Western Hemisphere and making clear that this is an American hemisphere.
It is the Republicans in this body, in particular, and the Senate that had to end-run Democrats who did not want to fund ICE and Border Patrol.

They refused to appropriate money for the law enforcement agencies tasked with ensuring our country is secure and required us to use the reconciliation process to backdoor funding to ensure that ICE and Border Patrol would get funded.
And I am proud of the things that I talked about and our position in the world and the secure border and the strong military.

The President's rationale was that he believed that rather than coming here and signing a housing bill that he wanted to make sure that this body, the House, and the Senate knows that he expects us to pass the SAVE America Act in order to secure our Nation's elections.
I don't think it should have included $200 million for an affordable housing pilot program from Congresswoman Tlaib.
I think what has made this Congress successful is sticking to our job of fiscal responsibility.

Holding our spending in check, stop increasing the debt, stop increasing the deficits, helping get interest rates down by driving down the deficits as a percentage of our gross domestic product, while the President drives up the economy, strengthening our military, strengthening our borders, doing the core constitutional functions of our Republic, that is what our job is.

I have been very clear that there is no comparison here between a party that wants to side with the woke agenda that is destroying our country, that wants open borders, that doesn't want to stand with our military, and that wants to undermine our President at every turn.
Number one, this Congress needs to pass codification of the President's successful border security provisions.
It would solve the problem of the abuses of parole, the abuses of asylum, and the catch and release policies that were abused under Biden.
Yes, the Senate may sit on it, like they are doing with the SAVE Act.
Let's codify the end of free healthcare and education under Plyler v. Doe and other taxpayer-subsidized public benefits for illegal aliens.
Let's defund the sanctuary jurisdictions.
We added 1 percent remittance fees on illegal aliens last year, in the big, beautiful bill.
Let's act as a body to end automatic birthright citizenship, even as we are looking at what the Court does.
There should not be birthright citizenship for just being born on our dirt.
There should be birthright citizenship for being born to an American citizen, mother or father.
Let's ban the entry of and remove foreign nationals who adhere to sharia law and undermine the rights of women.
Let's codify the elimination of foreign aid and expose the NGO funding, which is typically hostile to our interests.
Let's codify our exit from the World Health Organization that the President unilaterally executed from the executive.
Let's stop foreign aid for recalcitrant countries that refuse to take back illegal aliens.
Let's rapidly develop nuclear power.
Ban government control of American citizen spending by banning any central bank digital currency.

If you don't know what that is, Mr. Speaker, if you don't know what a CBDC, a central bank digital currency, is, it is the government being able to monitor and control your currency, your spending, and your dollars electronically and being able to say: Oh, no, you can't buy that gas now.

Let's ban government and corporate surveillance in our cars by killing the kill switch where we have mandated technology going into cars making them more expensive so they can monitor you and monitor your face while you are driving, Mr. Speaker.
Let's not forget why we are sitting at $40 trillion in debt to reduce deficits and debt.
We did a great thing in the big, beautiful bill by enforcing reforms to Medicaid and making sure that illegal aliens couldn't get welfare benefits in Medicaid.
That is an extraordinary piece of work that we have done, but we are not denting the debt yet.
Let's pass a balanced budget amendment.
However, don't send up to me, White House, a supplemental spending bill because of Iran for $87 billion with an E15 mandate in it.
Yes, we racked up debt after World War II, but we also did a lot of war bonds, we did a lot of rationing, and we had a lot of tax increases to deal with the war.
Let's ban congressional stock trading.
I support term limits, but whatever.

My view is, though: Why are you here day trading and engaging in the active trading of stocks when you are voting on the very thing you are supposed to be doing for the American people and not yourself?
Let's defund abortion and Planned Parenthood like we did in the big, beautiful bill and transgender surgeries.
Let's stop mifepristone and the pill that is going around killing literally hundreds of thousands of unborn babies.
Let's defund and limit that mifepristone.
Let's not empower government to police speech.
Let's protect American land and housing from foreign ownership, and let's pass a constitutional amendment for term limits.
If we can't pass a constitutional amendment for term limits, then why don't we just say we are not going to provide pay for Members after a certain period of time?
I am not saying my bill on banning congressional stock trading is the only way or the right way.
We have been talking about passing a balanced budget amendment for a long time.
We have talked about term limits for a long time.
We have talked about what we need to do to secure our country and secure our border.
Can we start with something like codifying border security?
Can we ban congressional stock trading?
I am going to get into some disagreements in a minute, and I am going to get into some things that I think we ought to do.

We are not going to engage in endless wars, but we are, in fact, going to make sure that our enemies know who we are, what we are doing, and that they are going to listen and that they are going to come to the table.
I am going to highlight a few of those things and talk about some directions that I think we ought to go.
I don't know whether we will get it across the finish line by the end of this Congress or not.
I am proud to support and work to defend veterans.

We should send over the codification of what the President is doing, to address what I saw today, a bunch of immigrants and migrants in Mexico who are saying to the camera: We are going to wait till Trump is gone, and then we are coming.
I am not going to vote for that.
I am going to be leaving at the end of the year after four terms.
I introduced a bill to do that.

Mr. Speaker, I don't know if I will get a chance to get back down on the House floor next week before we celebrate our 250th birthday, but that brings up two things for me to recount in my last 2 minutes.

Finally, I remind us as we are celebrating the 250th birthday of this country and all the sacrifice of all of our forefathers who bled, died, and fought for it that we have an obligation to do the same for our kids and grandkids, or we will lose it.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: NATIONWIDE CONSUMER AND FUEL RETAILER CHOICE ACT OF 2025
statements.title: NATIONWIDE CONSUMER AND FUEL RETAILER CHOICE ACT OF 2025

Mr. Speaker, as the House of Representatives works to deliver on the critical issues our Nation faces, we urge our colleagues today to prioritize the passage of S. 1383, the Safeguard American Voter Eligibility Act, or the SAVE America Act, which builds upon the SAVE Act introduced in previous Congresses that requires States to obtain proof of citizenship for Federal elections, ensuring only U.S. citizens are voting in those elections.

When you have a trillion dollars of improper payments, when you have the State of California openly and publicly stating that they are gaming the Medicaid system and the provider tax and the Federal match rate to provide funds to illegal aliens and for their general budget to game the system at what best can be called money laundering, as was editorialized in The Wall Street Journal last week.

When that is what is happening, when you have people on Medicaid who are getting a higher subsidy than people on Medicare, who have paid into it their entire lives, into the tax on Medicare; when you have people who are able- bodied who are getting a higher subsidy than the vulnerable population for whom Medicaid was originally created, then someone explain to me why we don't have a duty to fix that.
That is the system that we are living with now under expanded ObamaCare.
That is what that is, expanded ObamaCare.

They want to talk about the expansion of that population into the able-bodied who could be and should be working at a higher rate of return by the Federal Government than is going to the vulnerable population, while California games the system to give money to illegal aliens.

They don't want to talk about how you manage that problem, how you get more people to be able to have affordable care instead of what they currently have, which is a broken system that insurance companies run, forcing individuals onto an exchange so they can get like my constituent who passed away last year from cancer, who wanted to go to M.D. Anderson and could not go because she was on an ObamaCare plan and couldn't go to the best cancer hospital in the world because she was covered under ObamaCare.
The gentlewoman from California (Ms. Pelosi), the former Speaker of the House, came down and described that somehow we are not factoring in the price of clean air.

In fact, worldwide, the extent to which coal-fired plants in China, coal-fired plants in India, and other countries around the world are producing CO2 and other particulate matter that is bad for the air is rising.
Why would we undermine our own economic well-being to pursue a negligible impact on the overall global emissions, while driving up the price of goods and services for the average American family?
There is a reason why, when I drive around Austin, Texas, I see it is the rich folk driving around in their Teslas.
It is the rich folk who are getting their EV tax credits.
They are out in the rich parts of Austin.
Mr. Speaker, 77 percent of the world's electric vehicle batteries are manufactured in China.

Immediately upon adoption of this resolution, the House shall proceed to the consideration in the House of the bill (H.R. 2753) to amend the Congressional Budget Act of 1974 to provide for a point of order against reconciliation measures that cut benefits for Medicaid or the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program, and for other purposes.
Mr. Speaker, I rise in support of this rule and in support of the underlying legislation.
I introduced the ARTICLE ONE Act to try to restrict Presidential power under the Trump administration the first time and had trouble getting it moved during the Biden administration.
That is, of course, the ``you did it, so we will do it'' argument--not particularly satisfying if you want to have an open body.
My point being, if we are going to change the body institutionally, then let's have a real conversation about changing the body institutionally.
I won't waste a whole lot more time on it.

Mr. Speaker, I support this rule, and I urge my colleagues to support this rule.

statements.title: BORN-ALIVE ABORTION SURVIVORS PROTECTION ACT
sentences: Mr. Speaker, pursuant to House Resolution 5, I call up the bill (H.R. 21) to amend title 18, United States Code, to prohibit a health care practitioner from failing to exercise the proper degree of care in the case of a child who survives an abortion or attempted abortion, and ask for its immediate consideration in the House.
Mr. Speaker, the Born-Alive Abortion Survivors Protection Act protects one of our most vulnerable populations; innocent children.
We are all too familiar with the horrors of abortion and the unchecked power of the abortion industry.
We know it is simply common sense to provide lifesaving care to those babies who survive an abortion.

She said: I was traumatized and changed forever by my experience of holding a little abortion survivor for 45 minutes until he died, a 21- or 22-week-old baby who had been aborted because he had Down syndrome.

This legislation is simple: The Born-Alive Abortion Survivors Protection Act requires that infants born alive under an attempted abortion receive the same protection under the law and degree of care of any newborn, combined with, by the way, the penalties associated with those who would ignore their duty under the law.

Last Congress, unfortunately, only one Democrat voted in favor of the Born-Alive Abortion Survivors Protection Act and another voted ``present.'' My Democrat colleagues send a clear message to the American people that these innocent lives are not worthy of protection and those who intentionally let infants die after birth should not be held accountable.

Mr. Speaker, I would note another abortion survivor, Melissa Ohden, testified before the House Judiciary Committee in 2015. ``You wouldn't know it by looking at me today, but in August of 1977, I survived a failed saline infusion abortion. . . .
Madam Speaker, I yield 3 minutes to the gentleman from New Jersey (Mr. Smith), my friend and co-chair of the Pro-Life Caucus.

Of course, those who have suffered through it, including the baby whom I described who was being held as it was dying for 45 minutes after such a grotesque procedure, beg to differ, as do the 143 babies whom the CDC, which is hardly a paragon of pro-life propaganda, writes that between 2003 and 2014 at least 143 babies died after being born alive.
We are not talking about abortion.
Mr. Speaker, I was just handed by my pro-life, female legislative director information here about pregnancy centers.
Private and public adoption agencies assisted approximately 115,000 adoptions in 2022.

Even though I disagree with her on a whole lot of issues, I was proud to sit with her and meet with her when she was being targeted for prosecution by the weaponized Department of Justice under Joe Biden to be put in jail because she is pro-life.

The fact of the matter, as my friend from Maryland and the last speaker is trying to allude to here, when we are talking about it is already against the law and it is murder on the books, here is the problem: Down here in the District of Columbia, we have the D.C. five, which were very clearly full-term abortions.
Biden's Department of Justice refused to look into this information, but the D.C. five reveals the uncomfortable truth about abortion and a reality that we are all dealing with here.
Mr. Speaker, Gianna Jessen, another adult survivor of abortion, testified to the House Judiciary Committee in 2015, stating: `` . . .
I was delivered alive in an abortion clinic in Los Angeles on April the 6th, 1977. . . .

We just heard one of my colleagues on the other side of the aisle describe very specifically, yes, what we are trying to say we shouldn't do, which is, after a procedure, an abortion or otherwise, if you have a living human being, that, yes, you should try to resuscitate and save that child.
She described having been a nurse, having witnessed what occurred where, in her testimony, the child was born after the abortion procedure.
That is why I rise in support of this legislation.

Again, I will note that my colleagues on the other side of the aisle will not address and do not want to address the simple purpose of this bill: protecting a living American from being allowed to die without having medical treatment provided to that child.

Had he been there, he would have ended my life with strangulation, suffocation, or leaving me there to die.'' I will have plenty to answer for when I meet my maker and talk to the good Lord, for my life as a flawed and sinful human being, but I will not have to answer for not standing up in every which way that I possibly can to stop those kinds of horrors and to stand up for a fellow living American, a fellow living human being allowed to die, for the political whims of my colleagues on the other side of the aisle.

statements.title: PARDONING PRO-LIFE ACTIVISTS TARGETED BY DOJ
sentences: These are individuals who are pro-life who had been put in jail because a weaponized Department of Justice was unleashed against these individuals, very specifically and purposefully because they were espousing their pro-life views.

If you look at the application of the so-called FACE Act that was used to prosecute these individuals, to arrest and prosecute them, 97 percent of the FACE Act prosecutions between 1994 and 2024 were initiated against pro-life Americans.

Ninety-seven percent of the prosecutions under this one act were carried out against pro-life Americans--this despite the fact that there have been numerous attacks on pro-life facilities and crisis pregnancy centers in the wake of Dobbs.
Ninety-one pregnancy resource centers have been attacked since the Dobbs opinion was leaked.
In 2022, pro-life activist Mark Houck was arrested by the FBI for FACE Act violations related to an incident outside of an abortion facility.

By the way, I think this is really important in the context of the speeches that my colleagues on the other side of the aisle were just giving with respect to the treatment of those individuals incarcerated, charged, and prosecuted in the wake of January 6.

Regarding these individuals whom I am talking about with respect to the pro-life prosecutions by the Department of Justice under Joe Biden, as one of the attorneys for one of the defendants put it: ``While Biden's prosecutors almost entirely ignored the firebombing and vandalism of hundreds of pro-life churches and pregnancy centers, they viciously pursued pro-life Americans.'' ``And had they been opposing anything but abortion, Joe Biden would have given them medals.

Instead Biden wanted them branded as convicted felons and imprisoned for years in a Federal penitentiary.'' Eva Edl is an 89-year-old survivor of a Soviet concentration camp who sat in front of the entrance to an abortion clinic in a wheelchair.

Again, I want everybody to understand who is listening to this at home: An 89-year-old survivor of gulags in Europe was prosecuted by the Biden Department of Justice at age 89 for being in a wheelchair in front of an abortion clinic--a Federal crime, Federal Department of Justice.
It is because she was at an abortion clinic professing her faith and her hope that they would not carry out abortions.
Lauren Handy is a peaceful, pro-life activist and was formally sentenced to 57 months, almost 5 years, plus 3 of supervision, for her efforts to peacefully save the lives of the unborn.
She was protesting an abortion clinic.
I want to follow up, though, on my colleagues here who took the floor regarding January 6.
I was very clear on this House floor 4 years ago during January 6 that what occurred was wrong.

Mr. Speaker, when you literally go prosecute an 89-year-old gulag survivor because she was exercising her pro-life views at an abortion clinic, what do you think one's view is of the righteousness of the other actions of the Department of Justice?
It is because today the President righted the wrongs of those 21 individuals who were literally protesting, in their view, and I share that view, the murdering of unborn children.
May I remind my Democratic colleagues that the individual who burned down a police station, a career criminal, got 27 months.
There was an executive order declaring a national emergency at the border.
In the first Congress that I was in office, I introduced the Border Visibility and Security Act to help regain operational control of the border.

I put together a bill calling on the designation of cartels as foreign terrorist organizations, and I am pleased that that was one of the President's executive orders this week, declaring cartels as foreign terrorist organizations.
He issued an executive order requiring Homeland Security to deport aliens with orders of removal.
There is an executive order to end the catch-and-release program and an executive order to resume the successful migrant protection protocols and return to Mexico, so we can stop the flow.
To reinstate recognition of title 42 where you cannot travel through the country with communicable diseases.

An executive order ending birthright citizenship, as it has been applied wrongly and incorrectly for years, to people who have manufactured or have used a manufactured cottage industry in which people pay money to get delivered into the country, have a baby, get the citizenship, and then it is what is known as anchor babies.

From my reading of the law, when the 14th Amendment was passed in 1868, a mere 4 years later, the United States Supreme Court in the Slaughterhouse Cases, explicitly said--4 years removed from the passage of an amendment to the United States Constitution, the then-sitting Supreme Court said that it did not apply to people who were here as the children that were being born here of people who were foreign citizens.
One court came in and said: Well, no, we think there is birthright citizenship if you are born here to a foreign national, but only if you are a legal permanent resident.
I believe this Supreme Court will side on the right side, which is that you are a citizen if you are the child of an American citizen.
Subject to the jurisdiction thereof has to matter.
The President is restoring our border, restoring law and order, and reversing the damage, and he should be.

President Trump, 78 hours in, has been withdrawing us from the disastrous World Health Organization, a globalist entity that has been undermining our sovereignty and wants to take away our own decisionmaking and make us subject to foreign powers on our health issues; withdrawing us from the disastrous Paris climate treaty that was making us beholden to China and foreign nationals and unable to advance and promote our own American energy.
By the way, had we not reversed all of that, we wouldn't have been adding fuel to the fire of Russia going into Ukraine, so to speak.

The President has been declaring a national energy emergency; unleashing American energy; opening up exploration; reversing Biden's ridiculous bans on offshore drilling; making it the policy of the United States to recognize two sexes, male and female; ending affirmative action and DEI in the Federal Government and trying to get us back to the actual view of a government that does not look through the lens of color or sex, but, rather, merit and hard work; and requiring that everybody actually shows up to work.
We have already seen a massive decline in the number of people trying to come across our border.
Maybe the cartels will say: This may not be the profit center that we have at the moment.
The Border Patrol met with the union this last week.
The defense needs to be modernized, built up after getting undermined and focused on all sorts of ridiculous woke and DEI policies.
We said we would raise the debt ceiling over 2 years, about $4 trillion.
We are not inclined to want to raise the debt ceiling, if it hasn't been noticed, but we will do it.
The President wants us to get that aside so Chuck Schumer can't play games with the bond market, so let's get rid of the debt, or let's increase the debt ceiling.
Let's get $86 billion for Border Patrol.
How about let's just apply Medicaid work requirements so that, if citizens are on Medicaid for able-bodied Americans--not all, but the able-bodied Americans--that they must work?
We can pay for defense, pay for Border Patrol, make our Medicaid system better, and reverse the ridiculous student loan bailouts which are giving money from one American to another.
We want to make sure that President Trump can deliver on the border, get the debt ceiling away from being used politically by Chuck Schumer, and so we put that plan forward.
Some of my colleagues here seem to want nothing but tax cuts and no spending cuts.
I will also hear a lot of my colleagues say: Yeah, I am for the spending cuts.

Whether it is President Trump's vision or views on tariffs, whether it is something else, there has to be some amount of revenue to pay for all of the promises and all of the programs that every politician loves to go home and run on.

Come in with somebody else's models and show me how the math is going to work out, that if we do all of these tax cuts and do no spending cuts, that somehow we are magically going to have deficits going down because it is just not going to be true in the aggregate.
I think I am running close on time, and I just want to close with this: Right now, we have $36 point whatever trillion in debt.

If all of my colleagues who want deficit neutrality or deficit reduction on the tax bill combined with spending cuts, being debated in reconciliation right now, if I win that fight that I am having right now with colleagues--because they are like, I don't know--the best we will get is the current deficit, that is how we would end up with exactly what we have right now of roughly $2 trillion deficits.
By the way, it will get worse because of the interest I mentioned if we keep financing and refinancing our debt, and interest goes up.
If we want to transform this country, we need to reduce the deficits, give the President what he needs to secure the border, and give us healthcare freedom.
We will see how this plays out in the legal system.
I mean, that is the question I am going to be asking everybody.
If we renew all of the tax cuts, which I support, but we don't offer any cuts correspondingly, we will add hundreds of billions, if not several trillion dollars of deficit spending.
I am asking for deficit neutrality on the tax bill.
My actual last point with, I think, 1\1/2\ minutes remaining, is that, if we are going to do anything at all in reconciliation on policy, we should be fighting for healthcare freedom.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: MATH ISSUES
statements.title: MATH ISSUES
sentences: For everybody watching what is happening to our country, what this current administration is doing to our border, to our national security, to our spending, to the state of our culture, to the rule of law in the streets, the use of lawfare, the abuse of power, this can't come fast enough for most Americans.
As we speak, interest rates are going up, our debt is getting refinanced at higher interest rates, and we have more debt that we are going to have to finance at higher rates.
How do you think we got to $36 trillion in debt?

We are told we are not going to touch any kind of reforms in healthcare or Medicare to drive down the price of healthcare so that we can save Medicare from its clear insolvency, and Social Security from its clear insolvency.

Right now, conservatives in the House Freedom Caucus are often maligned on the pages of publications as being the rightwing guys because oddly enough we believe in freedom, balanced budgets, and securing the border.

The House Freedom Caucus has proposed, put forward, a plan to raise the debt ceiling over $4 trillion over 2 years; fund the border at $86 billion, the request by the incoming administration and border czar Tom Homan; fund defense modernization at $200 billion plus-up, a separate fund through reconciliation, so we can modernize our defense and do what we need to do to beat China.
Medicaid work requirements and SNAP work requirements are $120 billion.

Again, I want to be very clear because here is what you are going to hear in the coming weeks: The House Freedom Caucus refuses to do a debt ceiling so reasonable Republicans are going to have to go cut a deal with Democrats to increase the debt ceiling, increase appropriations over our current spending levels, including defense and nondefense, and, oh, by the way, give a crud ton of money to California.

Maybe we should come up with another path forward to actually honor our commitments to cut spending and reduce the size and scope of government while we cut taxes, secure the border, and do the things we are supposed to do.
Because the forces in this town who want nothing but tax cuts and no spending cuts are telling you, you can't do it.

The lobbyists, the people in this town, Members of Congress are saying that we can't cut because there is some program, there is something in Medicaid, there is some reason, there is some excuse, but, gosh, we are definitely going to go ahead and reinstate all the tax policies because they read in some book a long time ago that they all pay for themselves irrespective, by the way, of the Laffer curve or any commonsense economics.
Show the American people the math, and don't go run and hide behind a vote on a balanced budget amendment because I promise you that is what my colleagues will say.
They will say, oh, man, we need a balanced budget amendment.
Pass a balanced budget amendment.
By the way, when all the people out there on Twitter say Chip Roy is railing against a balanced budget amendment, I would respond, no, I am not.
I am for a balanced budget amendment.
I can promise you every time we hit a debt ceiling, what will happen is we are going to raise the debt ceiling.
We will deliver spending cuts if we get in the room and work, but it is going to take time.
Do not risk border security by pushing it off months into the future.
Do the debt ceiling increase, do the funding for the border, and give it to Tom Homan tomorrow.
By February, they would have money for defense, money for the border and a fence, and a debt ceiling that is gone.

There are some of my colleagues who want to attach the border funding to the bills that we are moving forward without--they don't believe that we will get to the spending cuts that will make those of us who believe we need deficits to go down happy.
They want to try to force us to eat increased deficits in order to achieve the border security funding.
I don't think we should play games with the border security.
I don't think we should play games with getting the debt ceiling cleared off without giving more power to Chuck Schumer and Democrats to mess with us in March.

Let's make the 119th Congress be about success, delivering on the President's agenda and on the Republican agenda, the agenda we ran on, and, most importantly, delivering for our kids and grandkids a world in which they can actually live free from worrying about China, free from worrying about debt, and free from worrying about open borders and criminals on the streets.
I will save that for another day, notwithstanding the national championships coming up around the country which the University of Texas should be playing in.
The question before us right now as Republicans is whether or not we are going to deliver.

I promise you that we are going to be facing votes on this floor this year to extend the tax cuts that include, for example, child tax credits and other tax policies that in no way, shape, or form, economically speaking, pay for themselves.
We are going to be told to do that on faith, that the growth in the economy will magically produce revenue and cause deficits to go down.
What we are asking for for that is to reverse some of Biden's policies, which are all things that the President campaigned on.
I will tell you right now I would love to vote on a bill right now to just eliminate the tax code and zero it out.
Maybe we will do that before this year is over.
I started this speech by saying I support it, but I don't support it blindly.
I don't support it without recognizing our responsibility and our need to cut spending.

It is going to take time to undo the damage of the Biden administration and for us to go through everything that we need to go through to identify the cuts that we can all work through, but we will do it if we have the willpower to do it and if we can do math and understand that we need deficits to go down.

statements.title: ILLEGITIMATE COURT COUNTERACTION ACT
sentences: I thank him for his statesmanship on this particular issue, which is critically important for not just our friendship with our ally, Israel, but also our own national security, the protection of our own men and women in uniform.
It has taken unprecedented action of issuing arrest warrants for the sitting Prime Minister and former Minister of Defense of our friend and ally, Israel.
